summary: The Tabs file contains CSS for rendering navigation tabs and their appearance, specifically targeting the .tabnav element and its nested structures. The styles define layout, positioning, and visual presentation for primary and secondary navigation tabs, including selected states.
purpose: To provide visual structure and styling for tabbed navigation user interface components, ensuring consistent layout and visual cues for selected/unselected tabs.

workflows.name: Tab Navigation Rendering
steps: Apply .tabnav class to a container element to set base positioning and dimensions.
Render a nested unordered list (ul.secondary) for secondary tab navigation.
Each navigation tab is a list item (li) floated left for horizontal layout.
Anchor (a) elements inside li configure tab appearance and spacing.
The selected tab uses an additional .selected class for visual emphasis (bold, black text).

business_rules: The width for ul.secondary should be set (e.g., 55em) for compatibility with various browsers.
Only one tab should have the .selected class at a time for accurate user feedback.
conditions: If a tab is selected, it receives the .selected class, changing its font weight and color.
system_behavior: Tabs visually indicate the active selection by styling the .selected anchor.
All tabs are rendered horizontally, with no list markers and consistent padding/margin.
dependencies: The visual output is dependent on HTML structure adhering to the expected class hierarchy.
exceptions: Older browsers (Opera, older Mozilla, Konqueror) require an explicit width setting for proper rendering.
content_gaps: No information about dynamic behavior (e.g., tab switching logic, JavaScript integration).
No details about primary navigation tabs, accessibility features, or theming support.
